summary: ACME Corp (Dedicated): capacity saturation causing 503/429 during peak windows (us-east) — autoscaler hitting max / slow GPU provisioning
environment: prod (Dedicated) - primary region us-east, overflow attempts us-west
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports recurring request failures + elevated latency on their Dedicated pool during peak usage windows.
- Symptoms look like pool saturation: increased queueing, 503s from upstream timeout, some 429s (throttling) when the pool is hard at max concurrency.

Customer impact
- ACME production workload experiences intermittent errors in peak windows (approx 09:30–10:20 PT and 14:00–15:10 PT).
- Impacted endpoints: /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions via Redwood SDK.
- Business impact per customer: "We miss SLA for our own downstream customers when your endpoint spikes." (see customer comment on 2025-01-22)

Environment
- Deployment: Dedicated
- Customer pool: acme-dedicated-gpu-pool-03 (internal)
- Primary region: us-east
- Secondary region: us-west (configured but not taking load due to routing policy pin + capacity mismatch)

What we’re seeing
- Pool hits max replicas for multiple 10–20 minute intervals.
- Autoscaler attempts scale-out but provisioning backlog increases; GPU nodes not available quickly enough.
- Scheduler queue depth grows; p95 latency rises, then requests start failing with timeouts.

Customer-provided errors (snippets)
- 503: "upstream request timeout" (from Redwood gateway)
- 429: "rate limit exceeded: dedicated_pool_concurrency" (intermittent)

Example request IDs (from ACME)
- req_01HNH3R9QKJ2P4W1E6K6S9Z0M2 (503)
- req_01HNH3V2Z0A8K2W8Y7ZK3Q0P1N (timeout)
- req_01HNH40D6S9N3C2B5J1F8Q9R0T (429)

Internal quick triage pointers
- Dedicated pool metrics: queue_depth spikes correlate with node_count flatlining at configured max.
- Fleet events show repeated "capacity unavailable" for the requested GPU class in us-east during peak.

Requested outcome
- Stabilize throughput during peak and prevent 503/429.
- If we can’t guarantee peak scale-out in us-east, ACME wants clear guidance on (a) right-sizing reserved capacity, and/or (b) enabling safe overflow to us-west.

Taxonomy mapping (for reliability program / reporting)
- Proposed incident category: Capacity exhaustion / autoscaling (Dedicated)
- Contributing factors (likely): Fleet capacity constraint (region/GPU class), autoscaler max too low, routing policy pinned to region, burst not enabled.

Attachments
- ACME timestamps + request IDs included above; can ask for additional sampling window if needed.
comments: 2025-01-22 09:14 (Dev Patel, Support) — Acknowledged. Looping in Infra/Fleet for dedicated capacity check. Can you confirm: (1) target QPS during peak, (2) whether any recent workload change (new model, longer outputs), (3) if overflow to us-west is acceptable for non-PHI traffic?

2025-01-22 09:37 (ACME Corp, Customer) — Peak QPS is ~2.2x baseline (batch jobs + interactive). No model change, but we increased max_tokens from 512 -> 1024 last week. us-west overflow is acceptable for our non-regulated requests, but we pinned us-east because it was previously more stable.

2025-01-22 10:05 (Irene Choi, Infra/Fleet) — Looking at acme-dedicated-gpu-pool-03: autoscaler max replicas set to 48. From 09:32–10:11 PT we were at 48/48 with queue_depth > 2k and provision attempts failing due to GPU scarcity in us-east for A100-80GB. We did not have burst enabled for this pool. This aligns with capacity exhaustion, not a runtime crash.

2025-01-22 10:22 (Rafael Mendes, SRE) — Confirmed in dashboards: p95 latency climbs before error rate. Gateway errors are mostly upstream timeout after N seconds (queueing). Suggest: (1) temporary raise max replicas if possible in region, (2) enable burst to secondary region, (3) adjust routing policy to allow spillover based on queue depth.

2025-01-22 10:41 (Irene Choi, Infra/Fleet) — Action taken: enabled burst policy (limited) + added us-west capacity reservation for overflow. Also bumped max replicas to 56 (subject to fleet availability). ETA 30–60 min for warm capacity. Monitoring queue_depth + error rate.

2025-01-22 12:03 (Dev Patel, Support) — Update to ACME: We identified dedicated pool saturation (autoscaler hitting max) plus slow provisioning due to regional GPU scarcity. We’ve enabled controlled burst and increased max replicas. Next step is validating stability during the next peak window; we’ll share a capacity plan recommendation after we have 24h of data.

2025-01-23 09:58 (Sergio Costa, Observability) — Pulled last 24h: error rate improved but still a smaller spike at ~09:40 PT when queue_depth briefly exceeded threshold. Suggest raising scale-out aggressiveness (queue-based) and confirming us-west pool has identical model set + weights cached to avoid cold-start penalties.

2025-01-23 11:16 (Vanessa Ortiz, Fleet) — us-west nodes are up. Noted model cache warm-up caused initial slowdown; after warm, throughput stabilized. We should document for Dedicated customers: overflow region needs pre-warming for top models or they’ll see initial latency.

2025-01-24 08:27 (ACME Corp, Customer) — Yesterday’s peak was significantly better. We saw brief latency increase but no 503s. We did see a handful of 429s (single digits). What is the recommended committed capacity to avoid this entirely?

2025-01-24 09:10 (Irene Choi, Infra/Fleet) — Recommendation: increase reserved capacity by +12 GPUs equivalent for us-east peak (based on queue_depth and max_tokens change), keep burst enabled with us-west overflow for safety. Also propose adjusting customer concurrency limits (soft) to reduce 429s while we right-size. I’ll send a formal capacity plan to Support for customer-facing response.

2025-01-28 16:45 (Dev Patel, Support) — Resolution: Dedicated pool capacity was saturating due to peak demand + increased output lengths; autoscaler reached configured max and scale-out was constrained by regional GPU availability. Mitigations applied: raised max replicas, enabled controlled burst to us-west with pre-warm, and tuned autoscaling thresholds. ACME confirmed no further 503s in the last two peak windows. Closing as Resolved. Follow-up: incorporate into incident taxonomy as 'Capacity exhaustion / autoscaling (Dedicated)' and ensure support playbook includes overflow pre-warm guidance.
resolution: Mitigated by increasing autoscaler max replicas (within fleet limits), enabling burst + overflow capacity in us-west, and tuning queue-based scaling thresholds; validated by subsequent peak windows with no 503s and materially reduced latency spikes. Provided customer with right-sizing recommendation for committed capacity given increased max_tokens.
internal_notes:
Owner mapping: primary Infra/Fleet (capacity + provisioning), secondary Platform/Routing (overflow policy) if spillover rules need changes.

For taxonomy v1: this ticket is a clean example of category 'Capacity exhaustion / autoscaling (Dedicated)'. Contributing factors to encode: (a) autoscaler max too low vs new workload, (b) regional GPU scarcity, (c) overflow region not pre-warmed.

Metrics to backfill: time-to-mitigate (burst enabled + max replicas increased), time-to-permanent-fix (capacity plan + pre-warm runbook).
